knowledge.q: How does the calculator work?
knowledge.text: The calculator answers concrete questions with your numbers: how long to reach your goal, can you buy it, what to buy first, is it worth it? And My business plan turns your goal into a mission-by-mission schedule: what to do first, second, third, session after session, your next session, backup plans if things don’t go as planned, and tracking that rebuilds the whole plan after each session. Tell me your numbers and I’ll set up the right tool for you, or read the Tutorial.

knowledge.q: How does My business plan work?
knowledge.text: My business plan has its own questions: your goal (a purchase, an amount, or something to unlock with experience: rank, XP, reputation…), where you stand, how you make your money (your missions, or an amount per hour), what you need to buy first, and what matters to you. It gives you the schedule in order: first, second, third… session after session, with the fastest route found using your missions, your next session, and backup plans A, B, C if you earn less than planned. After you play, you enter what you have, the time played, and the missions and purchases done: the whole plan recalculates. Save it: its full sheet stays in My saved plans. Nothing comes from the actual game: these are your numbers.

knowledge.q: How does “Is it worth it?” work?
knowledge.text: “Is it worth it?” covers three cases: a just-for-fun purchase (it earns nothing: I look at what it costs you, what you have left and the delay to your goal), a purchase that unlocks activities, and a purchase that earns you extra. For the last two, I compare the situation with and without the purchase over the same play time: only what adds to what you were already earning counts, and I tell you after how many hours it’s paid back. Without numbers from you, I don’t make up earnings or prices.

knowledge.q: What are the calculator’s tools?
knowledge.text: The calculator has two sections. “My calculations”: eight tools, each answering one question (My goal, My activities, My play time, My purchases, What should I buy first?, Is it worth it?, My budget, Which purchase should I pick?). “My business plan” turns your goal into a mission-by-mission schedule. Everything works with your numbers, no account needed.

knowledge.q: What’s “My goal” for?
knowledge.text: “My goal” tells you how much play time you need to reach an amount, and in how many days you’ll get there. You enter what you have (“I already have”), what you want (“I want to have”), roughly what you earn per hour of play, and your play time per day. Tutorial example: $200,000 in your pocket, $1,000,000 as the goal, $100,000 per hour, 1 h per day → you still need $800,000, 8 h of play, 8 days.

knowledge.q: What’s “My activities” for?
knowledge.text: “My activities” ranks your missions: you enter what each one pays, what it costs, how long it takes and the cooldown before you can do it again, and the tool tells you what you earn by repeating it during your play time, cooldown included. The three examples A, B and C are already filled in: replace them with your real numbers.

knowledge.q: What’s “My play time” for?
knowledge.text: “My play time” suggests a schedule for your session: you say how much time you have (15 to 90 minutes), whether you play solo or in a group, and which activities you’re up for; the tool tells you what you earn and how far it moves you toward your goal. An unfinished mission pays nothing: the schedule never cuts a mission in half.

knowledge.q: What’s “My purchases” for?
knowledge.text: “My purchases” tells you whether you can buy something now, and if not, how much play time you need. You choose a page from the site (vehicle, weapon, business…) or enter a price, then what you have and what you set aside. A place or a region is something you visit: the tool doesn’t offer it as a purchase.

knowledge.q: What’s “What should I buy first?” for?
knowledge.text: “What should I buy first?” compares purchase orders: you add two or three purchases with their prices, the tool compares your order with the reverse order and prices from low to high, and tells you which one gets you everything soonest. It waits until you have the money before each purchase and compares play time, not how much you want each one.

links.label: Open What should I buy first?

knowledge.q: What’s “My budget” for?
knowledge.text: “My budget” splits your money between the things you want while keeping some set aside: you enter what you have, you count your purchases from “What should I buy first?” or split it yourself, and the tool tells you what you have left or what you’re short. It only looks at the money you have now, never what you’ll earn later.

knowledge.q: What’s “Which purchase should I pick?” for?
knowledge.text: “Which purchase should I pick?” puts two to six purchases side by side with the same starting numbers: price, whether you can buy it and when, how much you want it from 1 to 5, the play time it costs and, if you enter it, what it earns. You choose what matters most (want / price ratio, cheapest, fastest to get, fastest paid back, most wanted) and the answer says “For you, it’s X” with the reason.

links.label: Open Which purchase should I pick?

knowledge.q: How do I compare two pages side by side?
knowledge.text: In My purchases, every page in the catalog has a “Compare” checkbox: as soon as you check the first one, a “My comparison” bar appears below the cards, for up to three pages. The table shows what we know; a “not known yet” price stays empty, it isn’t zero. On the Vehicles and Armory section pages, you can also check up to three cards with “Compare”.

knowledge.q: What’s the difference between Simple, Step by step and Expert?
knowledge.text: The three modes give the same answer with the same numbers: they change how you fill things in and read them. Simple shows the answer sentence, the numbers behind it and your next step; Step by step asks one question at a time and explains why; Expert adds every setting (fees, cooldown, share…), the tables, the curves with clickable points, the break-even points and the comparison with a saved calculation. Switching modes keeps your numbers.

knowledge.q: What does “Changed in Expert mode” mean?
knowledge.text: A setting changed in Expert mode still counts in Simple: a “Changed in Expert mode” line says so above the tool so you don’t forget it. Going back to Simple doesn’t erase it. Each tool keeps its own mode.

knowledge.q: What do I put in “I already have”?
knowledge.text: “I already have” is the money you have in the game right now. It’s the same box in every tool: if you change it in one, it changes everywhere. “The money I set aside” is the part you don’t want to spend.

knowledge.q: What should I put in “I earn about”?
knowledge.text: “I earn about” is what you earn in one hour of play, once your fees are paid. Common mistake: entering your total money there. If you don’t know how much you earn, open “I don’t know how much I earn” in My goal, or describe your missions in My activities.

knowledge.q: What’s a mission’s reward?
knowledge.text: It’s the money you get at the end of a mission, before paying your fees. It’s not what you actually have left: that’s your earnings.

knowledge.q: What are earnings, or profit?
knowledge.text: It’s what you have left once your fees are paid. Reward $100,000, fees $20,000: your earnings are $80,000.

knowledge.q: What’s ROI?
knowledge.text: It’s what a purchase has earned you, as a percentage of its price: earned in the end ÷ price × 100. 0% means paid back; 100% means it earned twice its price.

knowledge.q: What does “paid back”, or break-even, mean?
knowledge.text: It’s the point when a purchase has earned you as much as it cost. In “Is it worth it?”, the calculator tells you after how many hours of play you get there.

knowledge.q: What’s the return?
knowledge.text: It’s what a sum you spend earns you over a given period. An amount per hour of play isn’t a return: you also need to say how long you use it.

knowledge.q: What’s the money set aside (reserve)?
knowledge.text: It’s the part of your money you don’t want to spend. The calculator never touches it: it acts as if that money didn’t exist for your purchases. If you set aside more money than you have, the tool asks you to fix it.

knowledge.q: What does “You still need…” mean?
knowledge.text: “You still need $X” is the difference between what you want (or the purchase price) and what you can spend (what you have, minus the money set aside). If you entered what you earn per hour, the tool adds the play time needed to close the gap: “that’s 8 h of play”. Without that number, it asks you to enter it.

knowledge.q: How do I fix an empty field or a rejected number?
knowledge.text: Enter a number, for example 25000 or 25,000.50. Durations, prices and “I already have” can’t be negative. The message under the box says what’s missing. For an amount, you can enter 200k, 1.5 million or $200,000.

knowledge.q: Why does no activity fit in my play time?
knowledge.text: Check its duration including prep, the fees to pay upfront, the players it needs and the activities checked. An activity only pays once it’s finished: with 30 minutes, only short missions fit. An activity built for 4 players won’t fit if you play solo: check “In a group” and enter how many of you there are.

knowledge.q: Why does my result change in several tools?
knowledge.text: “I already have”, the money set aside, your purchases, and your activities are the same everywhere. Changing a purchase’s price also changes your budget, your buying order, and “Is it worth it?” Save a copy to compare two versions.

knowledge.q: Why do Simple and Expert give the same result?
knowledge.text: The mode changes what you’re shown, not the calculation. Expert lets you change extra settings; going back to Simple doesn’t erase them.

knowledge.q: Why isn’t a page’s price known?
knowledge.text: Rockstar hasn’t published any in-game prices: until it does, every page shows “not known yet” and you enter the price you imagine. The calculation becomes a personal simulation, never game data. An edition’s price in euros isn’t an in-game item price in dollars.

knowledge.q: What does “Restore the site price” do?
knowledge.text: When a page has a known reference price and you’ve entered a different one, “Restore the site price” puts the page’s price back. A price you enter yourself is “my own number” in the Tutorial’s vocabulary: it never becomes confirmed GTA VI data.

knowledge.q: How do I start over from scratch in the calculator?
knowledge.text: In the workspace, under the mode choice, “Start from scratch” clears the boxes of the current calculation and “Restore the examples” brings back the example numbers; your saved calculations and plans stay as they are. “Undo” goes back right after an action. To erase everything, including your saved calculations, go to the Progress page.

knowledge.q: What does the calculator’s “Got a question?” field do?
knowledge.text: It recognizes keywords and some amounts to open a tool and fill in fields. Always check the values it picks up: it doesn’t look up official earnings and can’t guarantee it understands every sentence. As for me, Léo, I do the same thing with more context: give me your numbers.

knowledge.q: What numbers do I enter for an activity?
knowledge.text: For each activity: the reward, what you pay each time, the duration, the prep, the cooldown before you can do it again, your share if there are several of you, what you need to buy once before starting, and the number of players needed. You change them in “Change my activities’ numbers” (My activities) or directly in My play time.

knowledge.q: How do I say I’m playing in a group?
knowledge.text: In My activities and My play time, choose “I play solo / in a group” and enter how many of you there are (including you, from 1 to 100). An activity built for more players than your group doesn’t fit in the schedule, and your share of the reward is what gets counted.

knowledge.q: Is the suggested schedule the only possible one?
knowledge.text: No. The calculator tries lots of schedules and keeps the one that earns the most in your time, but a better one may exist. In Expert, “Why this schedule?” explains the choice, and “Same activity in a row, at most” limits repeats.

knowledge.q: What does “This session moves your goal forward by …%” mean?
knowledge.text: In My play time, this line only shows up if you entered a goal in My goal: it says what share of what you still need this session earns, what you’ll still need after it, and how many sessions and days are left at this pace.

knowledge.q: What’s a custom purchase?
knowledge.text: A custom purchase is a purchase with no page on the site: you enter its name and the price you imagine. It’s available in My purchases, What should I buy first?, Is it worth it?, Which purchase should I pick? and the business plan. The calculation stays your own simulation.

knowledge.q: Why can’t I buy a place or a region?
knowledge.text: A place or a region is a destination: you visit it, and nothing says you can buy it. So the calculator doesn’t offer it as a purchase; it accepts vehicle, weapon, business and residence pages, and custom purchases. You can open the map or the place’s page.

knowledge.q: What’s a just-for-fun purchase?
knowledge.text: A just-for-fun purchase earns nothing: in “Is it worth it?”, the calculator then looks at what it costs you, what you have left, the time to get your money back and the delay to your goal, then compares “Buy now” and “Wait”. Nobody puts a price on fun. For a car that earns nothing, leave 0 in “Earns me extra”.

knowledge.q: What do I put in “Earns me extra”?
knowledge.text: Only what this purchase earns you ON TOP OF what you were already earning, per hour of play. It’s your own number: the game promises nothing. Common mistake: counting what you were already earning without the purchase as earned thanks to it. Enter what you were earning before in My goal so the comparison is fair.

knowledge.q: What does “Time you use it” mean?
knowledge.text: It’s the number of hours of play during which you use the purchase. “Is it worth it?” compares with and without the purchase over that same time: a purchase paid back after 6 h isn’t worth it if you only use it for 4 h (“Not over 4 h”), and a purchase that costs as much as it earns is “never paid back”.

knowledge.q: How do I test a purchase from a page on the site?
knowledge.text: Every page has a “The calculator” card: on a business, “Is it worth it?”; on a vehicle or a weapon, “Can I buy it?”; on a residence, a safehouse or a place, “Do the math”. The purchase comes into the tool already filled in, with its price if the site knows it. Then “Add it to my business plan” makes it your goal.

knowledge.q: What’s sensitivity (20% less or more)?
knowledge.text: In Expert, “What if the number moves by 20%?” recalculates your answer with 20% less or more on the number that matters (what you earn, the price…). Clicking −20% or +20% uses that number. It’s a way to see whether your plan holds up when you earn less than expected.

knowledge.q: What’s “Three activities, the same goal”?
knowledge.text: In My goal, under “Which activity gets me to my goal the fastest?” (open in Expert), three activities show the same goal reached with each of your activities: same starting money, each activity with its own fees and durations. A label marks “Fastest of the 3” and “Cheapest to start”. It’s a guide, not a promise.

knowledge.q: How do I save a calculation?
knowledge.text: Give the calculation a name, then click “☆ Save this calculation”: it goes into “My saved calculations”. The “My calculations” button, at the top and bottom of the workspace, shows how many you have and opens them in one click. “Save a copy” keeps a new try without overwriting the other one. Each card has Open, Open the page, Rename, Duplicate, Delete and Compare. Everything stays in your browser.

knowledge.q: How do I compare two saved tries?
knowledge.text: Open “My calculations”, check “Compare” on two cards, then click “Compare these two calculations”: the two show up side by side, and a sentence tells you which one needs the least play time or leaves you the most money. In Expert, “Compare with a saved calculation” also shows the gap between your current calculation and a saved calculation from the same tool.

knowledge.q: What’s the sheet for a plan or a calculation?
knowledge.text: In “My calculations”, “Open the page” opens the calculation or the plan as a document: for a plan, the goal, the session-by-session schedule, the purchases, the backup plans and your progress; for a calculation, its answer and the numbers used. You can print it.

knowledge.q: How do I export or import my calculations?
knowledge.text: “Download my calculation”, at the bottom of “My calculations”, saves the current calculation as a file; “Export my progress” (Progress page) also includes all your saved calculations and plans. On the other device, import the file, read the preview, then choose Merge or Replace. Older compatible saves are carried over.

links.label: Back up or transfer my progress

knowledge.q: I deleted a calculation by mistake, can I undo it?
knowledge.text: Yes, right after: “Delete” shows the “Undo delete” button. After that, the calculation is no longer in the browser, unless you had exported your progress.

knowledge.q: How do I share a calculation?
knowledge.text: In the workspace, “Share” puts your calculation in the page address (after #plan=) and copies that link: whoever opens it sees the same numbers. If the calculation is too long for a link, the tool tells you to download it; if copying isn’t available, the full link stays in the address bar. Nothing is sent to a server.

knowledge.q: What questions does the business plan ask?
knowledge.text: Five questions: “What’s your goal?” (a purchase, an amount, or something to unlock with points), “Where do you stand?”, “How do you earn your money?” (your missions or an amount per hour), “Before your goal” (what you need to buy first) and “What matters to you” (balance, speed, safety, a deadline). Nothing is silently pulled from the eight calculations: a “Reuse my numbers from My calculations” button copies them if you want.

knowledge.q: What are backup plans A, B, C?
knowledge.text: The business plan always keeps backup plans: other ways to reach your goal (for example with a single mission, or at the pace you actually had after a session), with their time and their money. They stay there if things don’t go as planned.

knowledge.q: What does “Update my plan” do?
knowledge.text: After each session, you enter what you have now, the time played, the missions done and the purchases made: the whole plan recalculates. The recap compares planned and actual, the plan restarts from your real amount, and an “At the pace you actually had” plan shows up in the backup plans.

knowledge.q: How do I set a deadline in my business plan?
knowledge.text: In “What matters to you”, enter a deadline if you have one. The plan tells you if it’s doable at your pace; if not, it tells you what to change, for example “sessions of 1 h 45 instead of 1 h”. It’s not a promise: if a number changes, the plan is redone.

knowledge.q: Does the business plan handle a goal you unlock with experience (rank, XP)?
knowledge.text: Yes: the goal can be something to unlock with points (rank, XP, reputation… whatever word you want). You say how many you need, how many you have and what it costs afterward; the plan organizes your sessions to get there.

knowledge.q: What’s “Your next session”?
knowledge.text: It’s the summary of what you do in your next session: the missions to do, what you earn, what you buy afterward. The full schedule, session by session (first, second, third…), is below in the plan document.

knowledge.q: What’s the difference between My business plan and My progress?
knowledge.text: My business plan starts from a goal and your numbers, then gives you the order of the steps and the play time you need. My progress tracks items you check off on the site. Neither one reads a save from your console.
knowledge.dq: quell differenc entr entrepris plan progression

knowledge.q: Can a purchase be paid for with the money it earns?
knowledge.text: No: a purchase is never paid for with the money it will bring in itself. The plan waits until you have the amount before each purchase, then counts the extra money the purchase brings in for what comes next.

knowledge.q: What do the calculator’s charts show?
knowledge.text: In Expert: the curve of your money over time (with your real results in the business plan), the “With or without this purchase” curve and the payback in Is it worth it?, the budget bars, and the session schedule. Each chart has a title, axes, a legend and a table; on the curve, you can fix a real point in one click.

knowledge.q: What’s the Tutorial?
knowledge.text: The Tutorial is the calculator’s guide in 15 chapters: your first calculation, the modes, one chapter per tool with an example to try and “a common mistake to avoid”, your saved calculations, the business plan, sources and statuses, the words the calculator uses and an FAQ. Each exercise opens directly in the tool.

knowledge.q: Are the numbers in the examples the game’s numbers?
knowledge.text: No. The examples in the Tutorial and the calculator are numbers for you to change: none of them is an official in-game price or earning. Rockstar hasn’t published any economic numbers; you’re the one who enters yours.

knowledge.q: What’s the little calculator on the home page?
knowledge.text: The home page has a small “How long to reach my goal?” with three boxes (I already have, I want to have, I earn about). It uses the same engine as the full calculator, and “Calculate my goal” opens the tool with your numbers.

knowledge.q: Are my calculations saved without an account?
knowledge.text: Yes: your saved calculations stay in this browser, with no account. Clearing the site’s data can delete them, so export your progress from time to time to keep it or take it to another device.
